steps.text: Sixty-five hours into the operation...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The battle between the ducal alliance and the Nachzehrers is brutal.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Just farther ahead is Silverrock Bluffs. The Originium response is intense, and the vehicle has already been paralyzed.

options: Vina should be arriving at the front lines soon.
The Exemplars have a tough task ahead of them.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: When the Sighs of Kings and the Stone of the Sword become one, we'll be able to see it from our position.

options: 'Catastrophes be sundered'.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It's only a myth.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: When people see things that defy explanation, they tend to exaggerate and romanticize them when passing down those to generations.

options: The Sighs of Kings and The Shard–
The Victorians' 'shield' and 'spear'.
The Shard is an application of Originium on the same level as large-scale witchcraft devices.
And the Sighs of Kings is able to neutralize certain Originium reactions.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I see you've done your homework.

options: Originium is often likened to a 'chronic disease'.
To this day, the people of Terra's best solution to Catastrophes has been – and still is – to avoid them.
It is incredibly difficult for people to directly intervene in the mechanisms of Originium.
But, the Victorians have long mastered these tools to save themselves.
The origin of the Sighs of Kings lies not in Victoria, right?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The first time I saw the Sighs of Kings was deep within the palace of the Shahanshah in Sargon.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: People regard it as a symbol of the Aslan's royal authority and believe that it can protect any settlement or city. This is indeed true. It is able to neutralize Originium reactions to a certain extent.

options: Only to a certain extent?
You don't seem particularly concerned about that caveat.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: That's right. No matter how much effort the Sargonian casters put into unearthing and retrofitting it, it was nothing but a former city defense device.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: During the era in which it was put to use, Originium was not yet widely-available across the continent.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I trust that it will be able to temporarily put a stop to Amnannam and give the Feranmut's spine an opportunity to take off, but it is not an inhibitor that can completely seal Originium activity.

options: Have you been disappointed too many times over all these years?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Doctor... from your current perspective, what do you think Originium is?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: A phenomenon brimming with the unknown? A resource to exploit? Or, perhaps, a source of disaster and disease?

options: I can't say.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: You don't want to, because your answer would be 'all of the above'.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Originium has long been inextricably woven into everything we see – our environment, our technology, our culture, and even our bodies.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If a portion of a limb is necrotic, cutting it off might solve the problem. But, what if the problem stretches from beginning to end?

options: There are some people who see you as omnipotent.
Why are you... looking at me?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Doctor, you asked me if I've ever experienced disappointment.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Just once.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I allowed myself to become overly dependent on one person, made a series of poor judgments, and paid the price.

options: Are you referring to...?
(Sigh)

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: But, it doesn't mean that I'll stop believing.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It is difficult enough to rebel against the very foundations of our origins. To pin your hopes on just one technology... or one person, is utterly unrealistic.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor! Dr. Kal'tsit! Please take a look at this!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: There's a cave up ahead.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Someone's concealed the entrance.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Crude, twisted. One of the Confessarius illusions.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I'm sure we'll find a witchcraft altar at its deepest point.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We should go to where the Originium response is the strongest.

options: There's Originium everywhere.
This level of Originium activation is unprecedented.
How are you feeling, Amiya?
Logos, you're also an Infected. Do you feel anything abnormal?
Kal'tsit, will our medicine still work?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: No problem here, Doctor.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We have more important things to do right now. I can tough it out.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: I'd be lying if I said that these environmental conditions weren't affecting me at all.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: But, it's more than just Originium.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: It beats being completely unprepared.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Under the influence of Amnannam, Originium will come closer to its true nature.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The crystal clusters will merge with all things – living and dead – at an increasing rate, sealing that data inside in an assimilated form.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Originium can only store information within its own structure. As such, any assimilated individuals will completely lose the forms they had in life.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Some may see this as nothing more than instantaneous 'decomposition'.

options: Just like those who die due to an Oripathy outbreak...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: There are some parallels. In the case of these patients, after their consciousness disperses, their bodies will disintegrate into highly-activated Originium dust over a period of time.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Assimilation, on the other hand, condenses this entire process to the extreme.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Rhodes Island's technology can only delay cell-Originium assimilation rate from reaching a certain threshold. We are not able to truly erect a barrier that can stave off Originium.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Don't worry too much about that, Doctor. The Originium saturation rate in our current environment is far from an extreme level.

options: Is our situation not extreme enough still?
It's hard for me not to worry.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Right now, we can still breathe and move about.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: If we're quick enough to stop the Originium from spreading further, all hope is not yet lost.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Dr. Kal'tsit, Doctor, I can hear enemy movements.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Logos, please prepare to intercept the enemy.

steps.name: Confessarius Guard
steps.text: Intruders?!

steps.name: Confessarius Guard
steps.text: It's the Banshee and––

steps.name: Confessarius Guard
steps.text: Urgh!

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: There are quite a few guards, but they're not difficult to manage.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: There must be greater dangers yet lurking in the shadows. Doctor, please stay close to us.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: The interference of Confessarius witchcraft is making it hard for me to pinpoint the exact location – but the Blood of Teekaz is undoubtedly nearby.
Teekaz blood roused the first Originium from its slumber.
Over the millennia, the fate of the Sarkaz has been tangled together with Originium.
Amiya and Logos are suffering. Or rather, they've shouldered this pain the entire time just to come this far.
What about you, then? You think of all the times Kal'tsit had to suppress the words she wished to say.
You are not only a witness and a bystander. Surely, you share a deeper connection – with Originium, with this war, and with everything that's been going on.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: This is...

options: The Blood of Teekaz.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Duq'arael's obsession.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: This so-called pure blood is free of 'impurities'.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: By itself, it possesses no inherent power.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Amiya, cut off its connection to the altar.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Got it–

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Wait.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: ...Dr. Kal'tsit?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Mon3tr, attack the corpse of that guard over there!

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Howls)

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: There's another Mon3tr?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: No, there's more than just one – all those defeated Confessarius guards... weren't real guards at all!

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Near-perfect replicas.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Only he could decorate this cave... to look nearly identical to a real altar.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: This was a trap designed to lure us in.

options: Damazti.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Amiya, get behind me!

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Furious howl)
Mon3tr stands in front of you.
And you grip Amiya's hand tightly.
The Blood of Teekaz is collapsing along with the entire altar, the surrounding rock walls pressing ever closer.
The illusion is no more, but the shifting terrain is real.
The real altar must still be functioning. Originium continues to grow, and it will soon consume everything you see.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor!

options: This is...
...the Confessarii's den.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: We seem to have fallen to the deepest level of the false altar.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The Originium was shifting too fast, and I only had time to grab onto you.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I don't know where Dr. Kal'tsit and Logos are... There's too much Originium here, too much information. I can't sense them at all.

options: They're probably far away by now.
The enemy wanted to entrap us.
They want to stop us from destroying the altar.
But, you might still be the Confessarii's real target.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: What they want is the King of Sarkaz.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The ground is still shaking... Are the crystal clusters still spreading?

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Wait, that's...
A monster suddenly crawls forth from the Originium's depths.
The horns of a Wendigo. The body of a Gargoyle. The flames of a Diαblo.
You have seen these before, in the Confessarii's stone sculptures, of the various Sarkaz tribes.
But never before sharing the same body.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: His emotions... are chaotic.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I see only memories – fragmented, blurry, and mashed together...

options: Amiya, over there!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: There will be many more, Doctor.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: This is the cave that gave birth to them.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The Confessarii sculpted them from Sarkaz blood and Originium...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: And gave birth to these creatures.

options: Does this... make you sad?
Amiya...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: They're alive, Doctor.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: They aren't chunks of rock, or constructs of witchcraft. They are living beings.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But, they obey only the call of the Confessarius. They do not feel any pain, nor do they cry for their fate.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: People would normally call these creatures... 'monsters'.
That's right. Monsters.

steps.name: Salus
steps.text: Or alternatively... 'Chimeras'.

steps.name: Salus
steps.text: Who are you even mourning for?

steps.name: Salus
steps.text: For these mindless kin, or for yourself – the Chimera forced to wear a crown?

steps.name: Confessarius 'Chimera'
steps.text: (Roars)

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: The fight is about to begin.

options: Amiya, are you being affected in any way?
Damn, more Confessarius witchcraft!

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Doctor, I won't let the Confessarii trap me a second time.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I'm not so fragile as to let these illusions and nightmares get to me. That name, 'Chimera', is no different from those dream-interrogations. I've heard it many times before.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: I have no right to be here, if I let myself get shaken by that.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Beyond that, however... I swore that I'd never let my immaturity drag you down again.
A tiny crown appears above the head of the Cautus girl.
Black lines interweave and take form between her fingers.

options: Your connection with the King is deepening.

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: Perhaps...

steps.name: Amiya
steps.text: But, it might not be enough.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: ...Amiya.

steps.name: Confessarius Guard?
steps.text: Don't be in such a hurry to leave.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: These clones are nothing before my incantations, Damazti.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Or, as you once put it, 'it is time wasted'.

steps.name: Confessarius Guard?
steps.text: We remember. That performance, and that stroll.

steps.name: Confessarius Guard?
steps.text: We talked for quite some time.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: That day you at least still considered yourself a lord of the Royal Court, despite having a different appearance.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: What are you now?

steps.name: Confessarius Guard?
steps.text: We try to take on different identities.

steps.name: Confessarius Guard?
steps.text: But, these varying journeys have yet to provide us with an answer.

steps.name: Confessarius Guard?
steps.text: What we conclude is, the path has neither beginning nor end. It is a cycle.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: And you sought out death to prove it.

steps.name: Confessarius Guard?
steps.text: At death's end, is nothingness.

steps.name: Confessarius Guard?
steps.text: The myriad souls you speak of have said nothing to us.

steps.name: Confessarius Guard?
steps.text: Banshee, how did it feel to sound the bone whistle for us?

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: 'Shatter'.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: There's no end to them.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: This is all you can muster? You've lost a lot of bite after your first death.
The clone, destroyed by the incantation, does not dissipate into nothingness as before.
Instead, that body simply collapses, sinking into the Originium tides until it quickly disappears without a trace.
From it, a hand resembling a withered branch extends from within the crystal cluster.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: 'Sudaram'.

steps.name: 'Sudaram'?
steps.text: Banshee... You once killed me as well.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: On the battlefield, I am not one of you.

steps.name: 'Sudaram'?
steps.text: In Kazdel, I was ordered to kill those who betrayed the Royal Court.

steps.name: 'Sudaram'?
steps.text: You got in my way, and separated my head from my shoulders with your incantations.

steps.name: 'Sudaram'?
steps.text: You were but a child then, with a puerile voice.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: ...I remember you.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: The traitors you mentioned were a family of three who wanted to flee Kazdel in search of a peaceful life.

steps.name: 'Sudaram'?
steps.text: They swore an oath of fealty to the Royal Court.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: The Royal Court should never be held above ordinary Sarkaz. You may have been a war hero of Kazdel once, but I cannot allow you to slaughter civilians.

steps.name: 'Sudaram'?
steps.text: So, you chose Babel, and Theresa... all for the sake of your so-called 'ordinary Sarkaz'.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: That is the righteous path to the future.

steps.name: Babel Member?
steps.text: But even after she died, you still didn't return to Kazdel!

steps.name: Babel Member?
steps.text: You even helped those outsiders steal away the King of Sarkaz!

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: The inheritance of the King of Sarkaz was a decision made by Her Highness Theresa.

steps.name: Babel Member?
steps.text: You killed me with your own hands.

steps.name: Babel Member?
steps.text: When your incantations were coiling around my heart, strangling it... Haha, I couldn't believe it.

steps.name: Babel Member?
steps.text: After fighting alongside each other for so many years, whatever you felt towards me paled in comparison to those outsiders.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: The potted goldengrass you left behind on the ship is growing well now.

steps.name: Babel Member?
steps.text: After Her Highness's death, how many comrades did you slay with your own hands during the internal strife that engulfed Babel?

steps.name: Babel Member?
steps.text: The belongings left behind by so many people... I'm sure there's enough of 'em to fill your whole room, huh? Do you feel sorrow every time you look at that patch of grass I planted in that pot on a whim?

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: If I were to feel sorrow...

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: It would be because even death has denied you the solace you deserve.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Damazti, you were never so keen to dress yourself up as the 'dead' before.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: This exchange of words cannot provide you with any answers, nor can probing my emotions.
The dead do not respond.
They continue to emerge from the dark crystal clusters.
Many faces, some familiar, others not. All of them Sarkaz.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Your innate abilities are resonating with the information stored inside the Originium.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Seeing as how your powers have grown thanks to the Originium–
Logos raises one hand.
No incantations are needed – just a low humming sound from the vibrating of the rock walls.
In a heartbeat, all of the Damazti's clones are shattered.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: Just as expected.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: There's one left... the very last one.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: It's you.
The Vampire stands there in the cave's depths, his expression almost identical to when he stood atop the Feranmut's skull that day.
However, it is no longer fresh blood that roils around him as before, but rather clusters of Originium crystal.
Logos can feel the blood in his body stirring.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: The Sanguinarch of Vampires... Duq'arael.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: You're not like the others. I know this.

steps.name: Logos
steps.text: You are not one of the Damazti's avatars.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Lord Damazti, this portion of you decided to assist Qui'sartuštaj.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: No... We have no interest in helping anyone in particular. We are simply... searching for answers.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Kal'tsit, we have met you before. When the Sarkaz were not yet Sarkaz.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: You walked across us.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I have no recollection of any such meeting.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: At that time, we were unable to speak.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: And then...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The first King of Teekaz came in contact with Originium.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: That was our first 'awakening'.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: The first individual rose up from among us.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: We felt one another.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: We had existed for an unknown amount of time before that. But, it was only at that moment when we became aware of our existence.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Because we began to 'think'.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Originium will assimilate all lifeforms it comes into contact with.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Not just you. But also the original Vampires, Banshees, and Wendigos... All Teekaz have changed. You are approaching the form of another entity that once existed on this land.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: Then, what are you?

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Howls agitatedly)

steps.name: Mon3tr?
steps.text: It seems extremely averse to seeing another self.

steps.name: Mon3tr?
steps.text: Kal'tsit... the Immortal.

steps.name: Mon3tr?
steps.text: Do you still remember what you looked like at first?

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The 'Immortal' is a figment of certain people's imaginations, and a misrepresentation of my self.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Time leaves its marks upon me all the same. The original entity by the name of 'Kal'tsit' has long been lost beneath the golden sands.

steps.name: Mon3tr?
steps.text: But, you are still yourself.

steps.name: Mon3tr?
steps.text: We were watching as you were reborn at Theresa's side.

steps.name: Mon3tr?
steps.text: You are different from your previous self, from your appearance to your personality.

steps.name: Mon3tr?
steps.text: We are used to constant change for the sake of survival.

steps.name: Mon3tr?
steps.text: Among the Sarkaz, the Damazti Cluster is unique. We once thought that you were like us.

steps.name: Mon3tr?
steps.text: We know many 'Kal'tsit', just as Kal'tsit knows many of us.

steps.name: Mon3tr?
steps.text: However, we will always be a whole. Each Damazti is a receptor for us to feel this land.

steps.name: Mon3tr?
steps.text: But, 'Kal'tsit' is different. Each Kal'tsit is still you.

spans.text: But, 'Kal'tsit' is different. Each Kal'tsit is still

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I do believe that to be true.

steps.name: Mon3tr?
steps.text: Why?

steps.name: Mon3tr?
steps.text: Is it the inheritance of memory that makes you so persistent? Memory can be easily tampered with and implanted. This, we know, for many long-lived beings have tried such methods.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Such 'immortality' is nothing but an empty lie.

steps.name: Mon3tr?
steps.text: Then, is it some kind of duty...

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: I won't deny that my life has been duty-bound from the moment I was born.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Looking back, I don't think... I've ever truly been 'alive'.

steps.name: Mon3tr?
steps.text: The substances that make up your body have all been replaced. The memories inherited from your previous self are unreliable. The mission imposed upon you may not even be your own.

steps.name: Mon3tr?
steps.text: Kal'tsit, what is it that has kept the continuity of you across these thousands of years?

spans.text: Kal'tsit, what is it that has kept the continuity of

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: A name.

steps.name: Mon3tr?
steps.text: A unique name, or a title? It is a question that so many emotionally deprived Sarkaz would be keenly interested in.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: This name, has many meanings.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: The person who gave me this name, and the people I care about, are now in danger. This isn't the time for us to be having this chat.

steps.name: Damazti Cluster
steps.text: We did not expect you to be this sentimental.

steps.name: Kal'tsit
steps.text: Mon3tr.

steps.name: Mon3tr
steps.text: (Excited howl)
